name: Butterscotch
lede: Butterscotch is a warm golden orange named, it seems, for the candy; Paterson defines it as a yellowish brown and also indexes it among the yellows.

sections.title: A candy that became a color
sections.body:
Paterson's color indexes list butterscotch among the yellows, next to butter yellow and buttercup yellow [1]. Paterson gives it its own entry, a yellowish brown, and does not mention the sweet, so the candy origin is an inference from the word itself [1]. The library finds the name in many systems, including RAL and Ridgway [2].

The swatch, #FDB147, is a saturated orange-yellow, whose nearest name is Marigold [2]. Compare [[apricot]], [[amber]] and [[orange]] [2]. Compare also [[caramel]] [2].

The name works as an everyday descriptor rather than a pigment, and the books consulted give it no history [1][2]. In LCH terms the swatch measures lightness 78, chroma 65 and hue 74 degrees [2]. The books consulted give no pigment behind the name [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 103 of 23,531 paintings, as photographed [3]. George Dawe has it in 9 [3].
